reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full MedicationKnowledge StructureDefinition report, the two direct behavior findings in the SearchParameters and HttpRestBehavior reports, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. I used the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level conclusion, as a comparison point rather than as the basis for the answer.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 MedicationKnowledge was trial-use/FMM 0, so the baseline stability pressure is weak and a substantial redesign is easier to justify than it would be for a mature or normative resource. That low maturity does not erase the compatibility concern: the resource identity disappears, the report cites real formulary-profile use, and several removed knowledge sections can carry medication safety or business-relevant content.

overall.oneLineConclusion: MedicationKnowledge is absent from R6 core, so a resource-level migration program dominates; compatibility value shifts to explicit transition artifacts and loss controls rather than isolated old element preservation.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual migration shape is a resource retirement plus decomposition, not a local remodel. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "MedicationKnowledge"` has no same-named R6 core StructureDefinition, no same endpoint/search surface, and no single replacement resource. Existing data must be classified into Medication, product-definition, Ingredient, ClinicalUseDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, extensions, or out-of-core knowledge artifacts before it can be R6-core valid.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: A major migration program is already unavoidable because validation fails at the resource identity boundary. The old resource combined product identity, ingredient information, monographs, related knowledge, cost, monitoring programs, administration guidance, classifications, packaging, regulatory facts, contraindications, and kinetics. R6 has partial homes for some of that content, but the reviewed inputs do not show a lossless one-resource successor or an official cross-version map. The most important migration work is therefore policy-driven decomposition and linkage of multiple resources, with explicit handling for knowledge-specific sections that do not have obvious core targets.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: This does lower the leverage of preventing additional isolated path-level breaks: keeping only `MedicationKnowledge.status`, old choice-arm names, or the self-reference target does not help if the whole resource type is gone. It does not mean compatibility has no value. The valuable preservation points are higher-level transition mechanisms: a deprecated compatibility resource or wrapper if the work group accepts the duplication cost, official StructureMap/ConceptMap guidance, standard legacy extensions for high-risk content, clear endpoint/search migration rules, and conformance tests that prevent silent data loss.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The main less-breaking base design would have retained `MedicationKnowledge` as a deprecated or transitional R6 resource, possibly as an aggregate wrapper over newer R6 resources. That would preserve old instances and IG dependencies, but it is not a low-cost alias: it carries a broad FMM 0 aggregate model forward and duplicates normalized medication/product-definition representations. Standard extensions for cost, monitoring, administration guidance, and kinetics would be a narrower mitigation for data loss, but would not by themselves make unchanged R4 instances valid R6 core content.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings are real but derivative of the resource removal. The R6 base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises a MedicationKnowledge REST endpoint, and SearchParameters whose only base was MedicationKnowledge disappear with the removed endpoint. Those should be handled in endpoint/search transition guidance for this resource family. Shared Resource and DomainResource findings, such as generic `$meta` and `$validate` changes, can affect generic clients but are context only for this resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent conclusion agrees with the deterministic aggregate on the top-level labels: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = Yes`, migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`. The important nuance is that this posture should not be read as dismissing the `Revisit` findings. The identity removal, split mapping, and knowledge-specific gaps still deserve standards/migration attention; the self-reference, status, and choice-shape findings are mostly local chores once the resource retirement is accepted.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the same R6 core resource is absent. Confidence is lower for the intended successor model because the supplied inputs do not include official pharmacy work-group migration notes, rendered R6 narrative guidance, a ConceptMap/StructureMap, or an example corpus showing which MedicationKnowledge sections are common in production. The R6 input is also a ballot package and should be rechecked against final R6.

findingConsiderations.title: MedicationKnowledge StructureDefinition is absent from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break. A valid R4 MedicationKnowledge instance cannot be accepted as the same R6 core resource, and generated resource classes, REST routes, validators, and profile dependencies lose the resource identity. Low FMM makes removal more defensible, but the blast radius is still high enough that a deprecated transition resource or explicit official migration surface deserves standards consideration.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 MedicationKnowledge content is split across several R6 model surfaces with no lossless one-resource mapping
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This explains why the resource removal is not a simple rename. Migration must decompose one aggregate into several R6 resources and choose linkage and loss policy. That makes a migration program unavoidable even if a local system used only a subset of MedicationKnowledge.

findingConsiderations.title: Several R4 knowledge-specific sections have no obvious R6 core destination in reviewed candidates
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Cost, monitoring programs, administration guidance, and kinetics are the strongest data-loss concern. They are not just syntactic fields; they can affect formulary, medication-use, monitoring, and clinical decision-support workflows. These gaps still matter even when the broader redesign is accepted, because migration guidance must prevent valid-looking R6 output from silently dropping them.

findingConsiderations.title: The local self-reference to MedicationKnowledge has no R6 core target
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Medication-knowledge graph links may be important for implementations that used them, but this path has no low-cost standalone preservation path once the resource identity is removed. Preserving it mostly means retaining a deprecated MedicationKnowledge target or defining successor-resource relationship rules, so it is a migration-design chore rather than an independent reason to change the resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 choice elements and generated classes cannot be carried forward mechanically
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generated R4 properties such as `itemCodeableConcept` or `valueString` need explicit typed transforms to R6 CodeableReference, Ingredient, ClinicalUseDefinition, product-definition properties, or extensions. This is a real SDK and FHIRPath migration issue, but preserving the old choice names would require retaining the old resource or duplicate fields.

findingConsiderations.title: MedicationKnowledge.status uses a removed value set and only partially aligns with R6 status semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Status is modifier information, so it should not be blindly string-mapped even though the lexical codes overlap with `Medication.status`. The right mitigation is target-specific status mapping and audit/provenance preservation where semantics differ. This matters for safe migration but does not independently justify preserving the removed resource model.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: MedicationKnowledge queries have no same-base R6 endpoint or same-base SearchParameter definitions. The break is operationally important for clients, but it is derivative of the resource removal and should be addressed by resource-specific query mapping, redirects/aliases where feasible, or explicit unsupported-endpoint guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: MedicationKnowledge is among the removed advertised endpoints, so generic conformance clients and route generators lose the REST surface. This confirms the API side of the identity break, but it does not create a separate migration shape beyond the removed resource and should be reviewed with endpoint transition policy.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: A MedicationKnowledge implementation that also used generic Resource metadata operations could be affected, and the operation-level review may deserve preservation. Under the resource-review rules, however, shared Resource behavior is context only because MedicationKnowledge is not Resource or DomainResource.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can affect generic validators during migration testing, but it is inherited operation behavior rather than a MedicationKnowledge content-model change. It should not be counted as additional MedicationKnowledge-specific migration pressure.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish an official MedicationKnowledge R4-to-R6 migration map that identifies target resources, linkage patterns, required extensions, and loss policy for every major R4 section, especially cost, monitoring programs, administration guidance, kinetics, related knowledge, and status.

Revisit the transition design for the resource identity removal. If retaining a deprecated R6 `MedicationKnowledge` compatibility resource is too costly, provide an explicit replacement package of standard legacy extensions, StructureMaps/ConceptMaps, and IG guidance so existing formulary and medication-knowledge users have a predictable migration target.

Define MedicationKnowledge endpoint and search migration guidance, including whether old REST/search routes are unsupported, redirected, aliased by implementation policy, or mapped to specific R6 resource families and query codes.

Create migration regression tests covering all R4 status codes, each R4 choice arm, self-references, and instances containing cost, monitoringProgram, administrationGuidelines, or kinetics so transforms cannot silently drop safety or business-relevant content.

caveats: The supplied inputs did not include an official R4-to-R6 diff, pharmacy module migration rationale, ConceptMap, StructureMap, or rendered narrative guidance for MedicationKnowledge.
The conclusion is based on the supplied R6 6.0.0-ballot4 core package; final R6 publication could restore or replace artifacts.
No production corpus was reviewed, so prevalence of specific MedicationKnowledge sections is unknown.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context and were not scored as MedicationKnowledge-specific findings.
